title: Unrestricted arithmetic lower bounds for the discrete Fourier transform
formal: Must computing the length-n discrete Fourier transform require Ω(n log n) arithmetic operations, even when n is a power of two and constants are not bounded in magnitude?
context:
The full card must fix its straight-line-program model. Bounded-coefficient lower bounds and counts of multiplications alone do not settle the unrestricted total-operation question.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Tests whether the central FFT upper bound is inherently necessary in unrestricted arithmetic computation.
